'''Marjorie Diane Blasius Corcoran''' (July 21, 1950 – February 3, 2017) was an American [[particle physics|particle physicist]] and professor at [[Rice University]].<ref name="hchron">{{citation|url=http://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/houston-texas/houston/article/Beloved-Rice-scientist-dies-in-bicycle-accident-10907787.php|newspaper=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=February 3, 2017|first=Mike|last=Glenn|title=Beloved Rice scientist dies in bicycle-light rail accident}}.</ref>

==Biography==
Born as Marjorie Blasius, she grew up in [[Beavercreek, Ohio]], graduating from [[Beavercreek High School]] as co-valedictorian in 1968.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/42845356/|title=485 To Graduate From Beavercreek High Tuesday |newspaper=Xenia Daily Gazette|date=May 27, 1968}}.</ref>
To begin her higher education, in 1972 she completed her bachelor's degree at the [[University of Dayton]], graduating ''summa cum laude.''<ref>{{citation|url=http://ecommons.udayton.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=5047&context=news_rls|title=Marjorie D. Blasius Graduates from the University of Dayton|date=May 8, 1972|work=Press release|publisher=[[University of Dayton]]|access-date=2017-02-04}}.</ref>
That same year she married Christopher Corcoran, taking his surname.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/10469682/|title=Marriage Applications|newspaper=Xenia Daily Gazette|date=August 9, 1972}}.</ref>  As a graduate student at [[Indiana University Bloomington]], she began doing high-energy physics research at [[Fermilab]].<ref name="hchron"/> Her 1977 doctoral dissertation, ''Measurement of the polarization parameter in proton-proton elastic scattering for beam momenta ranging from 20 GeV/c to 200 GeV/c'', was supervised by [[Homer Neal]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://library.nd.edu/physics/resources/genealogy/physics/documents/CorcoranMD.pdf|work=Notre Dame Physics Academic Genealogy|title=Marjorie Diane Blasius Corcoran (1950 – )|publisher=University of Notre Dame, Chemistry/Physics Library|access-date=2017-02-04|date=March 2, 2012|archive-date=2017-02-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170205182600/http://library.nd.edu/physics/resources/genealogy/physics/documents/CorcoranMD.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref> After earning her Ph.D. in 1977, Corcoran continued studies for 2 years at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2017-02-06 |title=The department mourns the loss of Professor Marj Corcoran of Rice University |url=https://www.physics.wisc.edu/2017/02/06/the-department-mourns-the-loss-of-professor-marj-corcoran-of-rice-university/ |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=Department of Physics |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/Online/22103/Marjorie-Corcoran |title=Marjorie Corcoran |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=pubs.aip.org}}</ref> She joined the Rice University faculty in 1980, where she would continue to teach for 37 years.<ref name="hchron"/> At Rice, she was the first speaker of the Rice Faculty Senate upon its formation in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rice mourns loss of Professor Corcoran |url=https://news2.rice.edu/2017/02/03/rice-mourns-loss-of-professor-corcoran/ |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=news2.rice.edu}}</ref>

She died while bicycling to work on February 3, 2017, in [[Houston]], from a collision with a [[METRORail]] train.<ref name="hchron"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Marjorie CORCORAN Obituary (1950 - 2017) - Dayton, TX - Dayton Daily News |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/dayton/name/marjorie-corcoran-obituary?id=18667475 |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref>

==Contributions==
As a professor at Rice, Corcoran continued her work at Fermilab as part of several large collaborative physics projects
including the [[D0 experiment]], KTeV collaboration, and the muon-to-electron-conversion experiment.<ref name="wotm" />

She also worked in physics outreach activities that included founding the Houston [[QuarkNet]] Program for high school physics students and teachers. She helped to found the Women in Physics Group at Rice, sending undergraduates to physics conferences, and otherwise encouraging other women to participate in physics.<ref name="wotm" />

==Awards and honors==
In 1992, the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) named her as a [[fellow]] "for contributions to experiments studying spin asymmetries in hadronic collision".<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?year=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=2017-02-04}}.</ref> She was also awarded the Distinguished Scientist Award from the University of Wisconsin physics department in 2008.<ref name=":0" /> In 2015, the APS listed her as their January 2015 Woman of the Month.<ref name="wotm">{{citation|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/women/scholarships/month/2015.cfm|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|title=January 2015 Woman of the Month: Marjorie Corcoran, Rice University|work=2015 Women Physicist of the Month|date=2015|access-date=2017-02-04|archive-date=2017-02-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170206103514/https://www.aps.org/programs/women/scholarships/month/2015.cfm|url-status=dead}}.</ref>
